intro: Indonesia is a presidential republic and, since 1998, a democracy: one of the largest in the world, where more than 200 million people can vote.

chapters.title: President and parliament
text: The president is elected directly for five years and can serve two terms. Prabowo Subianto became president in 2024, after Joko Widodo, known as Jokowi, a former furniture seller who had served two terms.
The People's Representative Council makes laws. Together with a Regional Representative Council, it forms the People's Consultative Assembly, which can change the constitution.

chapters.title: Pancasila and the motto
text: Pancasila's five principles are: belief in one God, a just and civilised humanity, the unity of Indonesia, democracy guided by wisdom, and social justice for all.
The national motto, Bhinneka Tunggal Ika, comes from an old Javanese poem and means 'Unity in Diversity'. The flag is red over white, and Independence Day is 17 August.

chapters.title: Regions
text: Indonesia has 38 provinces. Aceh, at the tip of Sumatra, has special autonomy and applies Islamic law, and in Yogyakarta the sultan also serves as governor. Papua has a long-running independence movement.

chapters.title: Indonesia in the world
text: In 1955 Indonesia hosted the Bandung Conference of newly independent Asian and African countries, which led to the Non-Aligned Movement. It was a founder of ASEAN, whose headquarters is in Jakarta, is a member of the G20 and joined the BRICS group in 2025.

keyTerms.meaning: The right of a region to govern some of its own affairs.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations, a group of ten (now eleven) countries.
